subject: Recap & MAP: Discovery with Cobalt Commerce — milestones, procurement path
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Thomas <ava@cobaltcommerce.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@cobaltcommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & MAP: Discovery with Cobalt Commerce — milestones, procurement path

Hi Ava / Tom —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and a proposed mutual action plan (attached) so we have alignment on next steps. I focused this summary on the decisions you said were most important to the team.

Key pain points you described
- Production recommendation latency spikes during promos (95th pct latency ~1.2s) impacting conversion; current infra struggle under burst traffic.
- Unit inference cost is high because models are hosted on general-purpose GPUs and CPU fallback is used for tails.
- Security/data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region for GDPR controls (this came up for EU merchant cohort).

Business goals (what success looks like)
- Reduce per-request inference cost by ~35–45% while keeping 95th pct latency under 400ms for promo traffic.
- Run a 6–8 week pilot with real traffic (shadow mode -> canary -> pilot).
- Procurement signoff and security review completed before pilot kickoff.

Proposed mutual action plan (attached: Cobalt-MAP-v1.xlsx) — highlights
1) Week 0–1: Security questionnaire + SOC2 artifacts exchange — owner: Procurement (Cobalt) / Vanessa (Redwood) — target: 2028-05-21
2) Week 2: Shadow traffic run (Redwood Dedicated) — owner: Ben (SE) / Cobalt infra — target: 2028-06-04
3) Week 3–4: Canary with 5% traffic; validate latency/cost SLOs — owner: Cobalt Eng / Redwood Ops — target: 2028-06-11
4) Week 6: Pilot review & decision (go/no-go) — owner: Exec sponsors — target: 2028-06-25

Asks from your side
- Confirm procurement contact (I also copied procurement@cobaltcommerce.com if you want to loop them in).
- Please review the attached MAP and the short list of required compliance artifacts.

Ben, Karthik — looping you both for the technical/milestone bits and to propose an initial sizing for the Dedicated pool.

Attachments:
- Cobalt-MAP-v1.xlsx (draft MAP: milestones + owners)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a short procurement sync if that’s helpful.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

[Attachment: Cobalt-MAP-v1.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)]

From: Ava Thomas <ava@cobaltcommerce.com>

Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@cobaltcommerce.com>, procurement@cobaltcommerce.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & MAP: Discovery with Cobalt Commerce — milestones, procurement path

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the MAP. High level: this aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- The latency target (95th <400ms) is critical for the checkout flow during promos; can you confirm which model variants you expect to use for the pilot and whether KV caching will apply to the recommendation model?
- Security: we’ll need SOC2 plus an explicit data flow diagram and confirmation that EU traffic can be pinned to an EU region.

I attached our RFP and the procurement contact (procurement@cobaltcommerce.com) — procurement will start their review today. Tom will coordinate infra access for the shadow run.

Proposed contacts:
- Procurement: procurement@cobaltcommerce.com
- Technical lead: Tom Li (tom.li@cobaltcommerce.com)

We’ll review the MAP and get back with any edits by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Ava
Head of Product | Cobalt Commerce
ava@cobaltcommerce.com

[Attachment: Cobalt-RFP.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]

Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap & MAP: Discovery with Cobalt Commerce — milestones, procurement path

Vanessa — thanks for sending. Quick technical / milestone notes from the SE side that we should fold into v2 of the MAP: 

Technical assumptions
- We’ll start pilot with a 8-bit quantized recommendation model (same architecture they run in prod). Quant + KV caching on the prefix should reduce cost ~30% in baseline; continuous batching for tail requests should get us the rest toward the 40% target.
- For EU residency: deploy a Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 and route EU traffic there; we’ll include a config toggle so Cobalt can lock routing per customer cohort.

Suggested MAP changes (to include in v2)
- Add explicit owner for infra access: Tom Li (Cobalt) / Ben Carter (Redwood SE) — ETA for infra credentials: 2028-05-20
- Sizing checkpoint: Redwood to provide initial Dedicated sizing (GPU count + throughput estimate) by 2028-05-18. Owner: Ben Carter
- Security artifacts delivery: Vanessa (Redwood) to deliver SOC2 extract + data flow diagram by 2028-05-20

Proposed milestone calendar (concrete dates)
- 2028-05-18: Dedicated sizing & cost estimate (Ben)
- 2028-05-21: Security questionnaire & SOC2 extract shared (Vanessa)
- 2028-06-04: Shadow traffic run (Tom/Ben)
- 2028-06-11: Canary (5% traffic)
- 2028-06-25: Pilot review & go/no-go

I attach an updated MAP draft (Cobalt-MAP-v2.xlsx) with the owners/dates filled in. I’ll also draft a short runbook for the shadow -> canary cutover.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

[Attachment: Cobalt-MAP-v2.xlsx (Excel, 52KB)]
